Visitors come for the sandy beach, ocean scenery and quiet relaxation by the shore. The Royal Decameron Punta Centinela hotel offers an all-inclusive option in the area; the specific services and accommodation conditions depend on the option selected.

Punta Centinela can easily be added to a trip after the Galápagos Islands, traveling via Guayaquil. A beach stop provides a chance to spend time without daily transfers. Seasonal excursions to observe marine wildlife are booked separately or included in certain tour programs.

Swimming and boat outings depend on ocean conditions. The image on this page is a created illustration of the coastline, not a photograph of a particular hotel.

A walk at Cormorant Point on Floreana begins with the unusual color of the sand. Tiny olivine crystals give the shore a greenish hue. Farther along, the trail leads to a brackish lagoon where flamingos can be observed. The birds slowly step through the shallows, dip their heads toward the water and leave barely visible ripples behind.

The small details are especially rewarding: reflections of pink plumage, changing colors in the water near shore, and low shrubs against the volcanic ground. The number of birds varies, so every visit depends on what the island reveals that day. A local guide can help spot lagoon wildlife and explain the features of the coastal environment.

On the other side of the point lies a pale beach of finely broken coral particles. The two contrasting shores make this short walk particularly memorable. Cormorant Point appeals to photographers and birdwatchers: it is a place to walk slowly and let your eyes adjust to the subtle colors of the island landscape.

### Punta del Este: Uruguay's resort city!

Punta del Este is an internationally renowned resort city where visitors can sunbathe on beautiful beaches and swim in the azure ocean, while also enjoying active leisure and a lively social scene.

## Beach holidays in Punta del Este

### Punta del Este: beaches, sea and sunshine!

The city offers numerous gyms and fitness clubs. Days revolve around the beach and ocean, while evenings bring a vibrant nightlife with plenty of nightclubs, restaurants and sidewalk cafés.

At Punta Espinoza, you first have to learn to tell the iguanas from the rocks. The dark lizards lie on the lava beside the water, gather in groups and lift their heads toward the sun. This point on the northeastern coast of Fernandina offers an opportunity to observe marine iguanas in their natural coastal habitat.

The walk crosses a small peninsula and stretches of lava. Flightless cormorants, sea lions and red crabs can be seen along the shore, while cacti grow near young lava formations. The rock itself is fascinating: smooth, hardened folds give way to rough fragments. Life gradually takes hold in cracks and small sheltered spaces among the volcanic stone.

Punta Espinoza is a rewarding destination for wildlife lovers and photographers. Take time to observe a single cormorant or a group of iguanas: after a few minutes, behavior becomes apparent that is easy to miss when walking past. Comfortable shoes for rocky ground make it easier to follow the trail and pause wherever the shore reveals more details.
